topics.topic: Allocation and primary ownership of A3 responsibilities across access modules and repositories
questions: Which exact part of A3 belongs to `viewer_access_repository`, and where is the boundary between that part and the viewer rows and project grants already owned by `viewer_access`?
Which exact part of A3 belongs to `service_identity_repository`, and where is the boundary between that part and the producer rows and grants already owned by `service_identity`?

After INV-009 is enforced independently by three access modules and three repositories, what single central mechanism makes `staff_identity` the primary owner of all A3 rather than making this part cross-cutting or splitting it into separately owned decisions?

Which exact parts of A3 do `viewer_access_repository` and `service_identity_repository` own, and which remain owned by `viewer_access`, `service_identity`, or the primary owner `staff_identity`—especially active-record lookup, historical-record retention, and enforcement of one active record per pair?

quotes:
Each accepted decision has one primary owner, the module that holds the decision's central mechanism, and consumers, except the two decisions recorded `cross_cutting` (A22, A26, below).
A consumer owns exactly the rules and parts of a decision its own section names; the primary owner owns every other rule of the decision.

The SQLite implementation of the `ViewerAccessRepository` port (the port itself is a `models` interface): client viewers, access credentials,
viewer sessions and project grants, with grant uniqueness.

Credential issue, revocation cascades or any transaction. It holds no
contact data (`ClientViewer` has none).

The SQLite implementation of the `ServiceIdentityRepository` port (the port itself is a `models` interface): service principals, service
credentials with their key versions, and producer grants.
Key-version allocation, scope decisions or any transaction.

The viewer rows of A3 and A11: ClientViewer creation and revocation,
ViewerAccessCredential issue (revoking every prior credential) and
revocation, viewer entry and session resolution, description and sign-out
(Factory `35a0a09ccbb1`), and project grants. Viewer session TTL is A30's.

A12 and the producer rows of A3 and A11: ServicePrincipal lifecycle,
ServiceCredential issue with monotonic key versions, rotation overlap and
revocation, producer grants, bearer authentication and producer scope.

A16 and the staff rows of A3 and A11: staff account creation by an
administrator, login and staff session issue, resolution and sign-out,
session revocation, status transitions with their cascade (sessions
revoked), password change, project assignment and its revocation, and the
administrative recovery override, the one replacement of a login email (A10,
Factory `3080ef0dbe73`). Session TTL is A30's.

The use case that owns an operation opens its transaction
through `portal_store`, closes it exactly once and guards it as A22 requires.

- **Rules:** at most one active grant per `(viewer_id, project_id)`; revoked
  grants of the pair stay as history. Revoking one grant affects only that
  project; Registry archival never changes grant status. A revoked grant is
  terminal and no operation reactivates it; giving the pair access again
  creates a new grant record.
  `revoked_at` and `revoked_by` are both null while the record is active and
  are both set, once, when it becomes revoked. No product operation lists
  revoked records: a read by pair returns the active record only, and the
  history serves the audit trail.

- **Rules:** at most one active grant per `(principal, project)`; revoked
  grants of the pair stay as history. A revoked grant is terminal and no
  operation reactivates it; granting the pair again creates a new grant
  record.
  `revoked_at` and `revoked_by` are both null while the record is active and
  are both set, once, when it becomes revoked. No product operation lists
  revoked records: a read by pair returns the active record only, and the
  history serves the audit trail.
judgement.why: The texts allocate lifecycle decisions and transaction sequencing to the identity use cases, persistence and uniqueness enforcement to their repository implementations, and residual A3 ownership to `staff_identity` under the stated primary-owner rule, while the models already specify active lookup and retained history.

topics.topic: Domain outcome, public response, and auditing for concurrent INV-009 uniqueness conflicts
questions: When two concurrent operations both pass the active-record check and one loses at the storage constraint, which module owns classification of that storage refusal, what operation-level outcome is returned, and does the losing operation write a rejected audit record?
When concurrent creation passes the operation-level check but loses at the storage uniqueness constraint, what typed/domain error and public response must the losing operation produce?

quotes: PortalUnitOfWork.commit: [ORCHESTRATION] Every implementation of PortalUnitOfWork MUST commit the complete write set of the unit of work atomically and exactly once and then close it, so no later call can use it; a failure MUST close it as well and surface as PersistenceError without driver detail.

PortalTransaction.commit: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST atomically commit the owned sqlite3.Connection complete write set, close the connection exactly once, enforce at most one active viewer and producer grant per respective pair, preserve exact expense allocation sums and section reference restrictions, and forbid update/delete of AuditRecord, SnapshotImportRecord, and ApprovedEstimateSnapshot; commit failure MUST rollback and close before raising PersistenceError.

grant_viewer_project: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST open its transaction with an explicit assignment, never as a context manager, because the transaction type provides no context-manager protocol and entering one raises TypeError before any read. It MUST reach viewer persistence only through the viewer_access repository of that transaction and append audits only with the imported append_audit into the audit repository of that transaction, use no legacy transaction-level viewer method, and close the transaction exactly once: a successful write commits once, a successful read rolls back once, and a failure rolls back only while the transaction is still open and re-raises the original failure unchanged.

grant_producer_project: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST re-raise the original failure unchanged and MUST NOT substitute a translated persistence error for it. Translating every failure turns a not-found or authorization rejection into a persistence failure, changes the answer the api gives for it and hides a defect from every caller and every gate; only a genuine storage failure is a persistence error.

Any other failure is 500. No failure becomes a success, an empty list or a
  zero, except in the two reads whose Errors say so:

The two rejected records of A13 (`snapshot.import`,
  `staff.login_failed`) are appended and committed in the refused
  operation's own transaction; every other refusal writes none.
judgement.why: The later transaction contract makes the losing constraint failure a `portal_store` `PersistenceError` mapped to HTTP 500 rather than the pre-check's duplicate-active refusal, rollback removes the attempted success audit, and State 3 independently says no rejected audit is written for this refusal.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
